subject: Request: DPA telemetry carveout + runtime analytics subprocessor — product/security signoff
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Sara Cho <sara.cho@pulseanalytics.com>, legalops@pulseanalytics.com
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: DPA telemetry carveout + runtime analytics subprocessor — product/security signoff

Hi Sara / Pulse legal,

Thanks for sending over the latest redline (attached). Pulse is asking for a carveout that allows Tracelytics (an analytics subprocessor they engage) to receive runtime telemetry and aggregated analytics from our inference runtime for performance monitoring and embedding-quality metrics. The key asks from Pulse: 1) include Tracelytics as a runtime subprocessor for telemetry, 2) telemetry retention of up to 90 days, and 3) a clause allowing use of anonymized embeddings/metrics for product analytics and model improvement.

Before we engage legal counters, I need Product and Security signoff on product impact and acceptable constraints. Marcus / Olga / Ben — can you weigh in on technical and security guardrails we should require (for example: retention limits, hashing/anonymization requirements, sampling thresholds, KV cache exposure risk, SOC2 requirement, encryption at rest/in-flight, dedicated tenancy)?

Attachments: DPA_Pulse_redline_v3.pdf, tracelytics-security-whitepaper.pdf

Goal: get internal alignment today so I can respond to Pulse with a single consolidated set of required changes and a follow-up DocuSign link.

Thanks,
Mina
Mina Haddad
Manager, Legal Ops — Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Sara Cho <sara.cho@pulseanalytics.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: DPA telemetry carveout + runtime analytics subprocessor — product/security signoff

Mina / Sara,

Thanks for flagging. Quick product notes from my side:

- Runtime telemetry: we can send aggregated metrics (latency histograms, error rates, token per request distributions) and sampling-based request traces. We should not send full request payloads or raw embeddings tied to user identifiers.

- Embeddings / model outputs: we can provide "derived metrics" (e.g., similarity aggregate stats) but not raw vectors unless Pulse signs an explicit training/derivative clause. The current redline language allowing "use for product improvement" is too broad — that would permit training on customer outputs which we generally disallow without additional commercial terms.

- KV/prefix cache risk: if any telemetry includes prefixes or partial KV cache content there is risk of exposing PII. We need a clause that disallows sending any cache content or request prefixes unless they are irreversibly hashed and sampled.

- Retention: 30 days is our default for telemetry sent to third parties. 90 days is negotiable but needs stronger minimization (e.g., must be aggregated to coarse buckets after 7 days). Proposal: allow 90 days only for aggregated metrics (no per-request identifiers), default 30 days for sampled traces, and require automatic aggregation/hashing after 7 days.

If Pulse can accept those constraints I think product impact is manageable. Otherwise we should push back on the carveout.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Product — Redwood Inference

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Sara Cho <sara.cho@pulseanalytics.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 13:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: DPA telemetry carveout + runtime analytics subprocessor — product/security signoff

Mina / team,

Security takeaways and required contract language:

1) Subprocessor minimums: Tracelytics must provide SOC 2 Type II (or equivalent) and a recent penetration test report. We should require a right to audit for high-risk customers and a subprocessors list that we review annually.

2) Data minimization & masking: No raw request/response payloads, no raw embeddings with direct identifiers. If Pulse insists on embeddings, those must be one-way hashed and only accessible in aggregated form. KV cache or prefix content is explicitly forbidden to be shipped.

3) Retention: Align with Marcus — default 30 days for any sampled traces, 90 days only for fully aggregated, non-identifiable metrics. After 7 days, all sampled traces must be aggregated or deleted.

4) Encryption/keying: TLS1.3 in transit and AES-256 at rest. Keys for telemetry data must be customer-segregated where possible — require KMS integration or dedicated keys for customers classified as high-risk.

5) Access controls & least privilege: Tracelytics accounts used by Pulse must enforce RBAC and MFA; no broad access to raw logs.

6) Data use: Add an explicit prohibition on training models on telemetry/embeddings without explicit written consent and a commercial agreement. The phrase "use for product improvement" is too permissive as currently written.

If Pulse accepts these, security can sign off. If not, we should reject the carveout and propose a telemetry-ping approach where Redwood scrubs/aggregates on our side and only pushes aggregated metrics to Tracelytics.

Regards,
Olga
Director, Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 14:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: DPA telemetry carveout + runtime analytics subprocessor — product/security signoff

Sara / Pulse legal,

Appreciate the patience while we reviewed this. Internally we've agreed we can consider a constrained carveout for Tracelytics provided the contract reflects the following non-negotiables:

- Tracelytics must be listed as a runtime telemetry subprocessor and provide SOC2 Type II evidence and a current pen-test.
- No raw request payloads, no KV/prefix cache content, and no raw embeddings tied to identifiers. Any embeddings must be irreversibly hashed and only used in aggregate.
- Retention: 30 days default for sampled traces; aggregated metrics may be retained up to 90 days but must be coarsened after 7 days.
- Explicit prohibition against model training on telemetry/embeddings without a separate signed agreement.
- TLS1.3 in transit, AES-256 at rest, and KMS-backed keys for customer-segregated telemetry where available.
- Audit clause: Redwood reserves the right to audit the subprocessor for high-risk accounts or on reasonable notice.

If Pulse accepts these edits I will have Legal finalize the redline and send a DocuSign link. If you prefer, we can also flip the integration so Redwood aggregates and pushes only aggregated metrics to Tracelytics (this is more secure but will add ~2 weeks to instrumenting dashboards).

Please confirm which path you prefer and Sara, if Pulse can provide the SOC2 report and pen-test link we can attach to the DPA and move forward.

Thanks,
Mina
Mina Haddad
Manager, Legal Ops — Redwood Inference
